main_text.l: crorum Antistites dicti sunt μύσαι mystæ, vel ἀπὸ τὸ
μύειν τὸ στόμα, os occludere, quia approbat, ut ait Eusta. τὰς μύσας μύειν στόμα, καὶ μὴ
ἐκφέρειν ἀμφὶ τὸ [illegible, ~8 letters]; Vel ab Hebr. מסתר [?] quod est occludere, unde מסתר [?] Ar-
canum. Hoc vocabulum postea Sacri Scriptores ab usu superstitioso tra-
duxerunt ad meliorem usum, ad designanda quæcunque Religionis Christia-
næ Capita, quæ carni & sanguini sunt abscondita. Sed in Scriptura nun-
quam usurpatur pro Sacramento, prout vox hæc strictè sumitur pro signis
fœderis Gratiæ; Quamvis de cætero vocem illam non repudiemus, quia
Sacramenta revera sunt rei arcanæ seu gratiæ invisibilis signa, quæ arca-
nam significationem habent, & latente mysterio sese potissimum commendant.
VII. Scriptura rectius vocat signa fœderis Gen. 9. 12. 13. & 17.
11. Signa & sigilla justitiæ fidei Rom. 4. 11. & signa simpliciter Exod. 12. 13.
ὑποδείγματα Heb. 8. 5. & 9. 23. & ἀντίτυπα 1. Pet. 3. 21. in Vet. Test.
nomen אות [?] occurrit Genes. 17. Exod. 31. Ezech. 20. quod signum notat,
& Sacramentis veteribus applicatur.
VIII. Licèt autem perfectè definiri non possit, quia est aliquid concre-
ti & extraordinarii, quod constat ex iis quæ non sunt in eodem genere;
potest tamen commodè describi. Multis dicitur signum rei sacræ, ex Aug.
qui dicit epist. 5. Signa quum ad res sacras pertinent Sacramenta vocari.
Scholastici definiunt, Sacramentum invisibilis gratiæ visibilem formam.
Sed neutra placet Pontificiis hodiernis, Bellarminus lib. 1. de Sacra. in genere
cap. 11. dicit has definitiones esse imperfectas, si accipiantur prout
verba sonant; si verò accipiantur secundùm sensum Ecclesiæ Romanæ
esse legitimas. Quia per signa intelligunt signa sensibilia, instituta & pra-
ctica. Nominatim ergo videtur duo reprehendere in definitionibus allatis.
1. Quòd Sacramenta dicantur forma visibilis nimis specificè, contendit
enim ad naturam Sacramenti satis esse, si signum sit sensibile, id est, ali-
quo sensu percipiatur, etiamsi non visu. Alterum quòd Sacramenta non
dicantur signa practica, id est, gratiam efficientia, quæ duo expressè ponit
in definitione Sacramenti, quam profert ex Cath. Concilii Tridentini his
verbis, Sacramentum est res sensibus subjecta, quæ vim habet gratiæ non
tantùm significandæ, sed & efficiendæ. Quod à Bellarmino callidè propo-
nitur, ut faveat commentitiis Sacramentis Pœnitentiæ, Matrimonii & si-
mi-mi, quæ carent signo visibili. Deinde ut sternat fundamenta falsæ illius
hypothesis, quòd nempe Sacramenta N. T. gratiam conferant ex opere
operato, ut loquuntur, de quibus in sequentibus.
IX. Nos in definiendo Sacramento Paulum sequimur, qui de Circum-
cisione loquens dicit esse signum & sigillum justitiæ fidei, Rom. 4. 11. quæ
definitio est generica, & rectè speciei tribuitur. Præluncente ergo hac fa-
ce, dicimus, Sacramenta esse signa & sigilla gratiæ Dei in Christo. Vel Pau-

page.notes: Note beside VIII: printed "Varie defi-nitiones Sa-cramenti."; the transcription above is in the margin note position "Varie definitiones Sacramenti" and is rendered as printed in the scan. Note beside IX: printed "Verè propo-nitur." Greek and Hebrew readings are uncertain. The Greek after "vel" in line 1 and the Greek in line 2 are blurred; the bracket after "ἀμφὶ τὸ" is illegible. The Hebrew in "vel ab Hebr." and "nomen" is marked [?]. Paragraph VII: "ὑποδείγματα" and "ἀντίτυπα" are read from the scan and marked as doubtful where the letters are unclear. Paragraph IX: "Præluncente" is read as printed and is doubtful; the scan is blurred at the start of this word. The line "Sacramentis Pœnitentiæ, Matrimonii & simi-mi" is printed as "& simi, quæ carent": the word "simi" closes a line and "mi" begins the next; the transcription keeps the hyphen as printed. Footer below the text: "Pars III." (left) and "13" (right, doubtful) are running-foot furniture, not catchwords, and are not in main_text. Heavy show-through and stains on the right margin and the lower left; no text in those areas was taken as printed.
